text:
Alex G: Heads-up — we have an enterprise customer reporting a bunch of 413s when they try to upload large embedding batches via our streaming/chunked path. They say it started after they switched to a single HTTP keep-alive stream and increased batch size. :rotating_light:
Maria T: Oof. Any repro payloads or logs yet?
Alex G: They sent a snippet and headers. curl looks like: ```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' --data-binary @payload.ndjson https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings/stream
```
Alex G: Server responds with 413 Request Entity Too Large mid-stream after ~9.5MB of data.
Sam R: 413 usually an upstream/body size limit (nginx/client_max_body_size) — but streaming should chunk. Is the client sending Content-Length?
Maria T: They are not using chunked transfer encoding; they are sending one large POST with NDJSON. That will hit our gateway limit.
Jess L: Can we confirm current gateway limit? I thought we had 10MB for non-chunked.
infra-sre: Current nginx config on the hosted cluster: client_max_body_size 10m. For streaming we accept chunked transfer-encoding; however some customers' proxies buffer and convert chunked into a single payload which triggers the limit.
Alex G: Customer is behind an enterprise proxy that buffers. So their single POST > 10MB gets rejected. They want to send 50k vectors in one go.
Sam R: That's not ideal. For embeddings we recommend batching by vector count or total payload size. We should give explicit best-practices: max ~1k vectors or ~4MB per request depending on dimension.
Maria T: Also saw a separate error in their logs: "dimension mismatch: expected 1024 got 1536" for a few requests. Likely they mixed models or serialized vectors wrong.
Jess L: Good call. Two distinct problems: (1) upload size limits causing 413s, (2) some batches contain vectors with wrong dimension leading to rejection.
Alex G: Need to send the customer a repro checklist and a short mitigation plan. Drafting here for review.
Maria T: Checklist: 
- Verify model embedding dimension (example: rwd-base-embeddings -> 1024 dims). Ensure client uses correct model.
- Validate each vector length before sending; drop/log any mismatched dims.
- Use chunked transfer-encoding or send NDJSON in multiple requests of <= 4MB compressed / <= 1000 vectors.
- If behind a proxy, recommend enabling passthrough or increase proxy buffer, or send smaller requests.
Sam R: Add: support gzip compression (Content-Encoding: gzip) for payloads to reduce size; we accept gzip on the hosted API. But note that some proxies disallow compressed bodies.
Alex G: Suggested temporary workaround provided to customer: split file into parts and POST sequentially, or switch to client SDK batch helper that does automatic chunking. Example Python NDJSON chunker: ```
def chunk_ndjson(lines, max_bytes=4*1024*1024):
    buf = []
    size = 0
    for line in lines:
        l = line.encode('utf-8')
        if size + len(l) > max_bytes and buf:
            yield b"\n".join(buf)
            buf = []
            size = 0
        buf.append(l)
        size += len(l)
    if buf:
        yield b"\n".join(buf)
```
Alex G: Also provided curl example using chunked transfer: ```
curl -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' --data-binary @chunk1.ndjson https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings/stream
```
Maria T: For the dimension mismatch: share a quick snippet for client-side validation: ```
def validate_vecs(vecs, expected_dim):
    bad = [i for i,v in enumerate(vecs) if len(v) != expected_dim]
    return bad
```
Sam R: If they still see 413s after chunking, ask for TCP capture or gateway logs. But first step: have them try smaller explicit batches (e.g., 200 vectors per request) and confirm success.
Jess L: Should we consider bumping client_max_body_size for hosted customers temporarily? Pros: quick mitigation. Cons: bigger memory footprint on gateway, potential DoS vector.
infra-sre: We can temporarily bump to 50m for that tenant using route-specific config. I'll schedule a short window and will notify infra. deploy-bot: Rolling patch to per-tenant nginx config queued (PR#4621). :white_check_mark:
Alex G: Nice. Also asked billing — they reported billing events failing around the same time but that may be unrelated; seems like two concurrent customer issues.
Maria T: Action items for support to send to customer: 
1) Run model-dim check and show sample of offending vector.
2) Try our SDK with default chunking or split into smaller NDJSON POSTs of <= 4MB.
3) If behind proxy, ask them to confirm proxy behavior (does it buffer chunked?).
4) If they need a higher single-request limit, we can escalate to infra for a per-tenant gateway increase (temporary).
Sam R: Also ask for the exact length/byte-size of the failing payload and the raw response headers from our API (we log x-request-id).
Jess L: I'll prepare the canned reply and attach the Python and curl snippets.
Alex G: Customer replied and attached a sample failing payload + x-request-id: rq_8f3b2a. They accepted trying split upload now.
infra-sre: I've submitted the per-tenant nginx increase request for that x-request-id; pending on-call review. If they want, we can enable streaming passthrough for their IP range.
Maria T: Good. Follow-up note: we should update support docs with concrete numbers: recommended max payload ~4MB (gzip ok), recommended batch size 200–1000 vectors depending on dimension, and include dimension validation snippet.
Sam R: Agreed. I'll add a short troubleshooting doc to /docs/support on Monday.
Alex G: Closing loop when customer confirms success. For now, marking as escalated to infra and providing workarounds. (reacted with :thumbsup:)
